topic: Mastering the Cross Product: From 2D intuition to 3D mechanics

sections.title: Prerequisite & The 2D 'Pseudo-Scalar'
sections.content: Briefly review vectors. Explain that in 2D, the 'cross product' is actually a signed area of a parallelogram. It represents how much two vectors are 'perpendicular' to each other, resulting in a scalar (magnitude only) indicating rotation direction (clockwise vs. counter-clockwise).
sections.example: Visualize a robotic arm in 2D: The cross product of the arm vector and the force vector determines if the arm rotates clockwise or counter-clockwise.

sections.title: The 3D Definition: Creating Space
sections.content: Transition to 3D: The cross product is a vector perpendicular to the plane formed by the two input vectors. Introduce the Right-Hand Rule (RHR) visually: Point fingers along vector A, curl to B, thumb points in the direction of the new vector C.
sections.example: Imagine a chameleon on a 3D grid: If its tongue extends along vector A and its tail aligns with vector B, the cross product vector shows the precise direction the chameleon must jump to stay perfectly balanced perpendicular to both.

sections.title: The Algebraic Formula (The Determinant)
sections.content: Present the determinant formula using i, j, k basis vectors. Explain that this mechanical method calculates the components (x, y, z) of the resulting vector. Keep the visual clean: a 3x3 matrix layout that reveals the cross-multiplication pattern.
sections.example: Calculate the cross product for vectors A=(1, 2, 3) and B=(4, 5, 6) step-by-step using the matrix expansion method.

sections.title: Geometric Meaning & Real-World Application
sections.content: Reinforce that the magnitude |A x B| = |A||B|sin(θ), representing the area of a 3D parallelogram. Conclude with a physics application: Torque. Torque = r x F, showing why applying force at 90 degrees yields the most rotation.
sections.example: A wrench tightening a bolt: The cross product of the wrench's length (r) and the hand's force (F) produces a torque vector pointing along the bolt's axis, causing it to move forward.
